scope: Userdata characterization for FUN_00cfa400's 4-metamethod metatable (cataloged structurally in BCS-Y-0502). Goal: identify the C++ type the userdata wraps.
outcome: Ghidra-resolved RTTI symbols directly name the wrapped type: Component::Lua::GameEngine::LuaControl (polymorphic base class) created by Component::Lua::GameEngine::LuaManyTentativeControlCreator (factory). The userdata wraps a 12-byte inner struct holding a LuaControl* pointer; all metamethod operations dispatch through the wrapped pointer's vtable. Read-only (the shared FUN_00ab7340 stub serves as __newindex). __gc invokes the wrapped LuaControl's release method (vtable slot 0) and frees the inner struct.

fields.name: control_ptr
fields.notes: Pointer to the wrapped LuaControl object. Set by FUN_00cfa400 after RTTI cast succeeds. Inspected by __index/__len for vtable dispatch and by __gc for release.

fields.name: slot1
fields.notes: Initialized to 0 by FUN_00cfa400. Possibly a weak-reference epoch token or auxiliary state.

fields.name: slot2
fields.notes: Initialized to 0 by FUN_00cfa400. Possibly a weak-reference epoch token or auxiliary state.

__index.behavior: Loads userdata, calls FUN_00cfc6d0 with stack-buffer (probably the dispatch lookup for the requested field name against the wrapped LuaControl's exposed interface). Not a hard-coded string compare like the individualref-userdata pass's _isAlive dispatcher - this is a general field-name dispatcher.

__newindex.behavior: Bare `return 0;` stub. Read-only - assignments are silently no-ops (no error raised, no state changed). Shared utility identified (BCS-Y-0502) for read-only Lua surfaces.

__len.behavior: Calls vtable slot +0x50 (= slot index 0x14 / 20) of the wrapped LuaControl. Returns the integer cast to double, pushed as Lua number. This is `#userdata` returning a virtual 'length' field of the underlying control - likely a child/entry/element count.

__gc.behavior: Two-stage destructor: (1) if control_ptr != 0 AND first dword of *control_ptr != 0, call vtable slot 0 of *control_ptr with arg 1 (= virtual `release(true)` or destructor-with-delete - the value 1 typically requests delete-after-call in MSVC vtable destructors). (2) _free(inner_struct). Note: passes only the inner-struct pointer to _free, NOT the wrapped LuaControl pointer - the LuaControl is presumably refcounted and the release call handles its actual destruction.

constructorPath.behavior: Iterator-shaped constructor. Treats param_2 as a 16-byte-stride vector (size check via `(end - begin) >> 4`), loads the element at *param_3, switches on a tag byte (local_14): tag 6 = push nil; tag 4 = proceed with userdata creation; other = throw std::bad_cast. For tag 4: RTTI-checks the element via dynamic_cast to LuaControl, vtable-calls slot +0x50 (verify), allocates 12-byte inner struct + 4-byte userdata body, installs the 4-metamethod metatable, increments *param_3. Probably the IMPL of a Lua iterator (next/__call) that walks a LuaControl container.
constructorPath.factoryUsage: RTTI cast targets BOTH LuaControl AND LuaManyTentativeControlCreator - the dynamic_cast checks if the source can produce a LuaControl directly, otherwise falls through. This is a polymorphism-aware factory dispatch.

ffxiv1xInterpretation: LuaControl appears to be a base class for Lua-accessible 'controllers' in the FFXIV 1.x engine - probably one subclass per game feature exposing its read-only state to Lua scripts (inventory list, equipment slots, party members, retainer state, etc). The 'Many Tentative Control' factory naming suggests this handles plural/aggregate results (lists of controls). __len returning a virtual count + __index dispatching field names + read-only __newindex is the classic 'view onto engine state' shape - Lua scripts read but cannot mutate. Mutation goes through dedicated N-APIs (the FUN_00cccad0 method-N-API surface) which then update C++ state via authorized paths. The corpus-napi-residual-findings/high-signal-napi-attribution-findings passes attributed many of those mutator N-APIs (`_setActorExtraStat` etc); this metatable is the READ side of the same model.
